deterministic.summary: HV loss was the BMS under-voltage protection acting (protective response, not the origin). Open upstream explanations: SOC estimation / calibration error; Usable capacity far below the stated parameter; Current under-measured or load bypassing the sensor. The recorded data does not separate them. A weak cell cannot explain the whole incident on its own: the highest cell was also depleted (pack-wide decline larger than the cell spread), and the SOC accounting discrepancy is pack-level: a weak cell can be an additional contributor, not the whole explanation. No root cause is confirmed.

result.headline: BMS under-voltage protection opened HV after SOC was abruptly restated 60.8%→22.8%; upstream cause not separable.
result.explanation: Cell voltage fell pack-wide while SOC, counted from a constant 6.54 A, stayed high. SOC then dropped sharply with no charge to explain it. SOC error, low capacity or a current under-read all fit.

evidence.quote: SHIFT battery.cell_voltage[min] changed level for good at t=640 s: median 3.2 before, 2.864 after V (2240x its variation before)
evidence.shows: Cell voltage fell at t=640 s while current stayed at 6.54 A and SOC stayed at 62.4 %. This is the earliest sign, long before any alarm.

evidence.quote: CHANGE battery.soc[bms] at t=1597 s: 43.2 -> 27.2 % (step -16, 10x its usual variation)
evidence.shows: Abrupt SOC re-statement. The charge accounting finds 37.95 pp unexplained in 30 s, with measured charge 0.0545 Ah.

evidence.quote: CONSTANT battery.pack_current held 6.54 from t=0 to 2100 s (4201 samples)
evidence.shows: Current was flat, so SOC counted from it was never going to track the real voltage fall. The energy shortfall is about 3.8 Ah delivered against 63.6 Ah promised.
Fault level 3 and contactor opening at the same instant, after level 1 at 1453 s and level 2 at 1799 s. This is the protection acting, not the origin.

evidence.quote: SHIFT battery.cell_voltage[max] changed level for good at t=640 s: median 3.21 before, 3.027 after V (915x its variation before)
evidence.shows: The highest cell fell too, so the whole pack was depleted, not one weak cell.

checked.check: Charge accounting: SOC against measured charge, reference and fault windows
checked.result: SOC tracked measured charge / about 100 Ah (ratio 1.101 and 0.892) except one 38 pp correction at t=1576.5–1606.5 s. The estimator was counting, with no visible voltage-based correction.
checked.about: SOC estimation / calibration error, usable capacity and current under-read all fit. The data cannot separate them.

checked.check: compare at t=640 s (voltage shift) and t=1597 s (SOC step)
checked.result: At 640 s no series stepped within ±15 s, so the voltage shift is a gradual level change. At 1597 s SOC moved 44.4 -> 25.6 while current was unchanged at 6.54 A.
checked.about: The SOC re-statement has no matching input change. No frozen output was found.

checked.check: sequence 600–2110 s with a 300 s baseline
checked.result: SOC left baseline first (1581 s), then max cell voltage (1976 s), then pack current (2100.5 s). The baseline window misses the earlier slow voltage fall.
checked.about: Cause and effect order. The current going to 0 at 2100.5 s is an effect of the contactors opening.

checked.result: Lowest cell was index 64 in 100 % of samples, but the highest cell fell 450 mV, more than the 260 mV spread. A weak cell cannot explain the pack-level SOC discrepancy.
checked.about: Weak cell / imbalance as the whole explanation

checked.result: The lowest-cell trace is smooth, the highest cell fell too, and the cells rebounded at rest. Contactors opened 0.0 s after fault level 3, not before it. Neither alternative is directly excluded.
checked.about: Cell-voltage sensing fault, and contactor/VCU first

checked.result: No lessons and no engineer-verified memory items apply.

effects.why: Contactors opened as the BMS protective response, 0.0 s after fault level 3. This shows how HV was lost, not why.

effects.quote: CHANGE battery.pack_current at t=2094.5 s: 6.54 -> 0 A (step -6.54, 1000x its usual variation)
effects.why: Current went to zero around the HV opening. The recording does not show who commanded the load off.
Escalation of the under-voltage protection, a consequence of the low cell voltage.

safety_findings.statement: Violation: SOC fell 37.95 pp in 30 s with no charge to explain it. Review the SOC estimator and its inputs before any further HV use.

unknowns: Whether SOC drift, low usable capacity or a current under-read caused the energy shortfall; the recording looks the same under each.
Cell series count, chemistry and protection thresholds are not given, so the protection sequence cannot be judged against a specification.
Charge and calibration history before t=0, and the real time between the two recording windows, are not in the data.

already_answered.question: Did the contactors open before or after the battery alarms?
already_answered.answer: After. Fault level 3 and the opening are at the same instant, following level 1 at 1453 s and level 2 at 1799 s.

already_answered.question: Was the load or current changing when SOC dropped?
already_answered.answer: No. Current stayed at 6.54 A through the SOC drop; it only went to zero around the HV opening.
